name: Patent Blue
lede: Patent blue is a deep greenish blue, the name of a blue dye used as a food colouring and in medicine.

sections.title: A dye with a number
sections.body:
Paterson defines patent blue as a deep greenish blue [1]. Patent blue V is the same blue, or bluish-violet, as a food colouring additive numbered E131, and it is also used for diagnostic purposes [1]. The same dictionary's patent yellow, a lead oxychloride pigment patented in 1781 by James Turner, shows the trade sense of *patent* [1]. That pigment was also called Turner's yellow and was a by-product of the soda industry [1].

It appears in the dictionary's list of blues, which also holds [[periwinkle]] and [[sky-blue]] [2]; for the older [[prussian-blue]], see its own page.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of museum paintings, a color near this swatch is present in 39 works, 0.16 per cent of the archive [3]. The earliest is a work from about 1387 and the latest dates from 1930 [3]. These are photographs of varnished paintings, so read them as screen colors [3].
